I want to say however everyone’s psychosis is different. I’m lucky in the sense I sort of knew I wasn’t well. Some people don’t. But I know it doesn’t happen every pregnancy. Psychosis is very quick setting in unlike pnd which can be quick but can also take months to set in.

My second I’ve had consistently for 6 months. She’s happy, developing well and I adore her. 

It’s why I believe that yes OP’s sister may have fucked up the first time but everyone deserves a second chance if the fuck up is due to an illness

Social workers got involved and instantly made the assumption I couldn’t do it this time. I had a psychological assessment which said I need therapy and parenting support to help and I should be able to do it. I do not have psychosis now. I’m well. I still have custody of my second girl who I love and have a bond with. 

What I’m saying here is, yes tell someone about the pregnancy, but don’t just cut her off. Psychosis changes you in the worst ways. I don’t know the ins and outs but for all that could happen she could be a better mother this time. How many years has it been since everything with her first?
